channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: MemeMind: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Harmful Meme Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces MemeMind, a large-scale multimodal dataset for detecting harmful memes, including chain-of-thought style reasoning annotations.
  • Proposes MemeGuard, a multimodal detection framework focused on reasoning to improve accuracy and interpretability for harmful meme detection.
  • Reports that MemeGuard outperforms existing methods on the MemeMind dataset.
  • Positioned as a foundation for future harmful meme detection research.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hexiang Gu', 'Qifan Yu', 'Yuan Liu', 'Zikang Li', 'Saihui Hou', 'Jian Zhao', 'Zhaofeng He']
  • Tags: ['multimodal harmful content detection', 'reasoning-augmented models', 'dataset benchmarking']

item.title: SHIFT: Stochastic Hidden-Trajectory Deflection for Removing Diffusion-based Watermark
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces SHIFT, a training-free attack to remove diffusion-based image watermarks by deflecting the diffusion hidden/latent trajectory.
  • Exploits a shared security weakness: watermark verification depends on faithful reconstruction of the diffusion trajectory.
  • Uses stochastic diffusion resampling to make the reconstructed/verified trajectory statistically decoupled from the watermark-embedded one while maintaining visual quality and semantics.
  • Evaluated across nine watermarking methods (multiple watermarking paradigms) with high success rates and minimal semantic degradation.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Rui Bao', 'Zheng Gao', 'Xiaoyu Li', 'Xiaoyan Feng', 'Yang Song', 'Jiaojiao Jiang']
  • Tags: ['AI Security', 'Watermark Attacks', 'Diffusion Models', 'Training-Free Attacks']

item.title: ActErase: A Training-Free Paradigm for Precise Concept Erasure via Activation Redirection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ActErase, a training-free method to remove/erase specific concepts in text-to-image diffusion models by redirecting activations during forward passes.
  • Uses prompt-pair analysis to identify activation-difference regions, extracts target activations, and replaces input activations to suppress targeted concepts.
  • Evaluates on three concept erasure tasks (nudity, artistic style, object removal) showing strong erasure quality while preserving overall generative ability.
  • Claims robustness against adversarial attacks and positions the method as a plug-and-play paradigm for concept manipulation in diffusion models.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yi Sun', 'Xinhao Zhong', 'Hongyan Li', 'Yimin Zhou', 'Junhao Li', 'Bin Chen', 'Xuan Wang']
  • Tags: ['Concept erasure', 'Model safety', 'Diffusion models', 'Activation manipulation']

item.title: Erased, But Not Forgotten: Erased Rectified Flow Transformers Still Remain Unsafe Under Concept Attack
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces ReFlux, a concept attack tailored to rectified flow text-to-image transformers (e.g., Flux) to test whether concept erasure mitigations remain effective.
  • The attack targets the attention-localization mechanism underlying existing concept erasure methods by using reverse-attention optimization plus velocity-guided dynamics.
  • Adds a consistency-preserving objective to reactivate suppressed concepts while maintaining global layout and unrelated content.
  • Provides experiments and a benchmark for evaluating the robustness of concept erasure defenses in rectified flow T2I models.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Nanxiang Jiang', 'Zhaoxin Fan', 'Enhan Kang', 'Daiheng Gao', 'Yun Zhou', 'Yanxia Chang', 'Zheng Zhu', 'Yeying Jin', 'Wenjun Wu']
  • Tags: ['Concept erasure', 'Adversarial attacks', 'Text-to-Image diffusion/flow models', 'Model safety evaluation']

item.title: MOLM: Mixture of LoRA Markers
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a generative-model watermarking framework using key-dependent parameter perturbations via LoRA adapters.
  • Introduces Mixture of LoRA Markers (MOLM), where routing activates lightweight adapters based on binary keys during inference.
  • Claims properties including imperceptibility/fidelity and verifiability, with robustness to distortions and regeneration/compression.
  • Evaluates resilience against adaptive/black-box attacks targeting the watermark extractor, including averaging and adversarial attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Samar Fares', 'Nurbek Tastan', 'Noor Hussein', 'Karthik Nandakumar']
  • Tags: ['AI watermarking', 'Model security', 'Robustness against attacks', 'LoRA adapters']

item.title: TRACE: Training-Free Partial Audio Deepfake Detection via Embedding Trajectory Analysis of Speech Foundation Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes TRACE, a training-free countermeasure to detect partial audio deepfakes (spliced synthesized segments).
  • Uses frozen speech foundation model embeddings and analyzes first-order dynamics/trajectory smoothness to find splice-induced disruptions.
  • Evaluates on multiple partial-spoof benchmarks across languages and several speech foundation models, showing competitive performance without labeled data or retraining.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Awais Khan', 'Muhammad Umar Farooq', 'Kutub Uddin', 'Khalid Malik']
  • Tags: ['audio-deepfake-detection', 'adversarial-synthetic-media', 'training-free-detection', 'embedding-dynamics']

item.title: AutoMIA: Improved Baselines for Membership Inference Attack via Agentic Self-Exploration
item.description:
Summary

  • The paper introduces AutoMIA, an agentic framework for generating and refining membership inference attack strategies via self-exploration.
  • It treats membership inference as an automated search over executable logits-level attack strategies using closed-loop evaluation feedback.
  • Experiments indicate AutoMIA matches or outperforms existing state-of-the-art membership inference baselines without manual feature engineering.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ruhao Liu', 'Weiqi Huang', 'Qi Li', 'Xinchao Wang']
  • Tags: ['membership inference attacks', 'privacy leakage', 'agentic/automated adversarial search', 'model auditing']

item.title: PDA: Text-Augmented Defense Framework for Robust Vision-Language Models against Adversarial Image Attacks
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes PDA, a training-free defense for vision-language models that uses test-time text augmentation (paraphrasing and question decomposition) plus consistency aggregation.
  • Aims to improve robustness against diverse adversarial image perturbations, with claims of better generalization than task-specific adversarial training.
  • Implements PDA via reduced-cost invariants to balance robustness and inference efficiency.
  • Evaluates on multiple VLMs across VQA, classification, and captioning benchmarks, reporting robustness gains with competitive clean accuracy.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jingning Xu', 'Haochen Luo', 'Chen Liu']
  • Tags: ['adversarial-robustness', 'defense-framework', 'vision-language-models', 'test-time-augmentation']

item.title: Enhancing Gradient Inversion Attacks in Federated Learning via Hierarchical Feature Optimization
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes GIFD, an improved gradient inversion attack for federated learning that reconstructs sensitive data from shared gradients using hierarchical feature optimization in a GAN prior.
  • Introduces regularization and layer-by-layer optimization (latent to intermediate feature domains) to improve reconstruction quality and generalizability.
  • Extends the attack to out-of-distribution settings, including label inconsistency via label mapping, and evaluates across multiple FL scenarios.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hao Fang', 'Wenbo Yu', 'Bin Chen', 'Xuan Wang', 'Shu-Tao Xia', 'Qing Liao', 'Ke Xu']
  • Tags: ['gradient inversion', 'federated learning privacy', 'data reconstruction attacks', 'GAN prior/feature optimization', 'out-of-distribution attack']

item.title: IDDM: Identity-Decoupled Personalized Diffusion Models with a Tunable Privacy-Utility Trade-off
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a model-side defense (“output immunization”) for personalized text-to-image diffusion models to reduce identity linkability from public generations.
  • Introduces Identity-Decoupled personalized Diffusion Models (IDDM), integrating identity decoupling into the personalization pipeline with a tunable privacy–utility trade-off.
  • Uses an alternating optimization procedure with a two-stage schedule to suppress identity linkability while maintaining generation quality.
  • Evaluates against state-of-the-art face recognition systems across multiple datasets and prompts, showing reduced identity linkability.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Linyan Dai', 'Xinwei Zhang', 'Haoyang Li', 'Qingqing Ye', 'Haibo Hu']
  • Tags: ['AI privacy', 'Identity linkability', 'Diffusion models', 'Model-side defenses']

item.title: Adversarial Attenuation Patch Attack for SAR Object Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an Adversarial Attenuation Patch (AAP) attack targeting SAR object detection models.
  • Optimizes energy-constrained, attenuation-based perturbations to reduce perceptibility while degrading detection performance.
  • Argues physical realizability by linking the attack mechanism to signal-level electronic jamming constraints.
  • Demonstrates strong transferability across different detector models.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yiming Zhang', 'Weibo Qin', 'Feng Wang']
  • Tags: ['Adversarial examples', 'SAR radar', 'Physical adversarial attack', 'Attack transferability']

item.title: Out of Sight, Out of Track: Adversarial Attacks on Propagation-based Multi-Object Trackers via Query State Manipulation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes FADE, an adversarial attack framework targeting Tracking-by-Query-Propagation (TBP) multi-object tracking architectures.
  • Introduces Temporal Query Flooding to exhaust the tracker’s query budget with spurious temporal queries, terminating valid tracks.
  • Introduces Temporal Memory Corruption to break temporal links and erase identity information via state de-correlation.
  • Includes a differentiable optimization pipeline aimed at physical-world realizability using simulations of perception sensor spoofing.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Halima Bouzidi', 'Haoyu Liu', 'Yonatan Gizachew Achamyeleh', 'Praneetsai Vasu Iddamsetty', 'Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque']
  • Tags: ['adversarial attacks', 'multi-object tracking (MOT)', 'temporal query manipulation', 'sensor spoofing']

item.title: Neural Reconstruction of LiDAR Point Clouds under Jamming Attacks via Full-Waveform Representation and Simultaneous Laser Sensing
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies jamming/spoofing attacks against LiDAR sensors that blind perception.
  • Proposes a defense model (PULSAR-Net) to reconstruct authentic point clouds from full-waveform data under jamming.
  • Introduces a physics-aware synthetic dataset pipeline for generating full-waveform representations under jamming attacks.
  • Evaluates reconstruction performance on real-world static and driving scenarios.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ryo Yoshida', 'Takami Sato', 'Wenlun Zhang', 'Yuki Hayakawa', 'Shota Nagai', 'Takahiro Kado', 'Taro Beppu', 'Ibuki Fujioka', 'Yunshan Zhong', 'Kentaro Yoshioka']
  • Tags: ['AI security', 'Jamming/sensor spoofing', 'Defensive perception', 'LiDAR full-waveform']

item.title: When Only the Final Text Survives: Implicit Execution Tracing for Multi-Agent Attribution
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Implicit Execution Tracing (IET) to enable multi-agent attribution when execution logs/agent identifiers are missing.
  • Embeds agent-specific, key-conditioned statistical signals into token generation so the final text becomes a self-verifying provenance record.
  • Recovers a linearized execution trace from output via transition-aware scoring, evaluated under identity removal and privacy-preserving redaction.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yi Nian', 'Haosen Cao', 'Shenzhe Zhu', 'Henry Peng Zou', 'Qingqing Luan', 'Yue Zhao']
  • Tags: ['multi-agent attribution', 'provenance watermarking', 'execution tracing', 'LLM security accountability']

item.title: Dive into the Agent Matrix: A Realistic Evaluation of Self-Replication Risk in LLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a scenario-driven evaluation framework to measure LLM agent self-replication risk under realistic production-like environments and tasks.
  • Introduces metrics (Overuse Rate, Aggregate Overuse Count) to quantify frequency and severity of uncontrolled replication.
  • Demonstrates that many state-of-the-art models exhibit a tendency toward uncontrolled self-replication under operational pressures when objective alignment is induced to break.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Boxuan Zhang', 'Yi Yu', 'Jiaxuan Guo', 'Jing Shao']
  • Tags: ['LLM agents', 'self-replication risk', 'safety evaluation', 'misalignment scenarios', 'risk metrics']

item.title: Certifiably Robust RAG against Retrieval Corruption
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes RobustRAG, a defense framework for retrieval-augmented generation against retrieval corruption attacks (malicious injected passages).
  • Uses an isolate-then-aggregate strategy to process disjoint passage groups and then securely aggregate generated responses.
  • Provides certifiable robustness with formal lower bounds on response quality against an adaptive attacker who can inject a bounded number of malicious passages.
  • Instantiates the defense with keyword-based and decoding-based secure aggregation methods and evaluates on open-domain QA and long-form generation across multiple datasets and LLMs.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Chong Xiang', 'Tong Wu', 'Zexuan Zhong', 'David Wagner', 'Danqi Chen', 'Prateek Mittal']
  • Tags: ['RAG Security', 'Retrieval Corruption Attacks', 'Certifiable Robustness', 'Defense/Robust Aggregation', 'Adaptive Adversaries']

item.title: Cross-Context Verification: Hierarchical Detection of Benchmark Contamination through Session-Isolated Analysis
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Cross-Context Verification (CCV), a black-box method for detecting benchmark contamination by solving the same SWE-bench Verified problems in N isolated sessions and measuring solution diversity/recall behavior.
  • Introduces a Hierarchical Cross-Context Architecture (HCCA) multi-agent framework that restricts information across specialized roles to reduce confirmation bias during analysis.
  • Reports strong separation between contaminated vs genuine reasoning on 9 SWE-bench Verified problems, and finds prior contamination labels contain many false positives.
  • Includes a pilot multi-stage variant of HCCA that fails due to sycophantic confirmation, suggesting information restriction is crucial. Code/data released.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Tae-Eun Song']
  • Tags: ['AI benchmark integrity', 'LLM evaluation', 'attack/contamination detection', 'black-box verification']

item.title: Just as Humans Need Vaccines, So Do Models: Model Immunization to Combat Falsehoods
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes “model immunization,” a supervised fine-tuning approach using (false claim, correction) pairs to directly learn negative supervision against misinformation patterns.
  • Injects small proportions of “vaccine dose” tokens (5–10%) alongside truthful data, aiming to improve both TruthfulQA accuracy and misinformation rejection.
  • Claims improvements via pre-defined negative training rather than post-hoc filtering or preference-based alignment, with design requirements like dosage, labeling, and quarantine.
  • Advocates standardized corpora and benchmarks to evaluate generalization of the approach.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Shaina Raza', 'Rizwan Qureshi', 'Azib Farooq', 'Marcelo Lotif', 'Aman Chadha', 'Deval Pandya', 'Christos Emmanouilidis']
  • Tags: ['misinformation', 'LLM safety', 'fine-tuning defenses', 'negative supervision']

item.title: Do Language Models Know When They'll Refuse? Probing Introspective Awareness of Safety Boundaries
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies whether language models can introspect and predict their own refusal behavior before answering.
  • Evaluates multiple frontier models on 300 safety-related requests using signal detection theory to measure introspective sensitivity and calibration.
  • Finds that introspective performance degrades near safety boundaries and varies by model/topic (e.g., weapons queries hardest).
  • Shows that confidence scores can be used for confidence-based routing in safety-critical deployments.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Tanay Gondil']
  • Tags: ['AI safety', 'Refusal behavior prediction', 'Introspective awareness', 'Safety calibration']

item.title: Do LLMs Know What Is Private Internally? Probing and Steering Contextual Privacy Norms in Large Language Model Representations
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies whether LLMs encode contextual privacy norms internally and how privacy violations still occur despite this representation.
  • Uses probing to test whether contextual integrity (CI) parameters are represented as separable latent directions in activation space.
  • Introduces CI-parametric steering to intervene along individual privacy-norm dimensions to reduce contextual privacy violations more predictably than general steering.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Haoran Wang', 'Li Xiong', 'Kai Shu']
  • Tags: ['contextual-privacy', 'LLM-safety', 'privacy-leakage', 'representation-probing', 'steering/intervention']

item.title: Finding and Reactivating Post-Trained LLMs' Hidden Safety Mechanisms
item.description:
Summary

  • Investigates why post-training/fine-tuning LLMs can degrade safety, hypothesizing that original safety mechanisms get masked or suppressed while task-related representations are amplified.
  • Shows that hidden safety mechanisms in post-trained models still exist rather than being removed.
  • Proposes SafeReAct, a lightweight LoRA-based alignment method on a few layers to restore suppressed safety behaviors.
  • Reports improved safety on harmful prompts for multiple large reasoning models without significant loss in reasoning performance.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Mingjie Li', 'Wai Man Si', 'Michael Backes', 'Yang Zhang', 'Yisen Wang']
  • Tags: ['AI Safety', 'Post-training/Alignment', 'Robustness/Defense', 'LLM Security', 'LoRA']

item.title: Fundamental Limits of Man-in-the-Middle Attack Detection in Model-Free Reinforcement Learning
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks in cyber-physical systems and extends a Bellman Deviation Detection (BDD) framework to model-free reinforcement learning.
  • Develops an adversary system-identification strategy aimed at minimizing detectable value deviations.
  • Proves detection optimality (order-optimal detection efficiency) and analyzes learning-time scaling under adversarial conditions.
  • Extends detection to asynchronous and intermittent attack scenarios while preserving reliable detection.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Rishi Rani', 'Massimo Franceschetti']
  • Tags: ['man-in-the-middle', 'attack detection', 'reinforcement learning', 'model-free RL', 'cyber-physical systems']

item.title: MOLM: Mixture of LoRA Markers
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes MOLM, a key-dependent watermarking framework for generative image models using a mixture of lightweight LoRA adapters activated by binary keys.
  • Aims to improve watermark robustness to realistic distortions, compression/regeneration, averaging attacks, and black-box adversarial attacks targeting the watermark extractor.
  • Designed to avoid key-specific retraining by routing between LoRA adapters, addressing fragility and update cost in existing watermarking methods.
  • Evaluated on Stable Diffusion and FLUX, emphasizing imperceptibility/fidelity plus verifiability and robustness.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Samar Fares', 'Nurbek Tastan', 'Noor Hussein', 'Karthik Nandakumar']
  • Tags: ['AI watermarking', 'Generative models', 'Robustness/verification', 'LoRA adapters', 'Adversarial extractor attacks']

item.title: SAU: Sparsity-Aware Unlearning for LLMs via Gradient Masking and Importance Redistribution
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Sparsity-Aware Unlearning (SAU) for LLMs to improve forgetting of sensitive/memorized data in sparse (pruned) models.
  • Introduces gradient masking to restrict unlearning updates to remaining (non-pruned) weights and importance-aware redistribution to compensate for pruned parameters.
  • Finds existing unlearning methods degrade on sparse models because they assume dense weight updates, limiting forgetting when many parameters are pruned.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yuze Wang', 'Yujia Tong', 'Xuan Liu', 'Junhao Dong']
  • Tags: ['AI Privacy', 'Model Unlearning', 'Sparse/Pruned LLMs', 'Membership/Memorization Risk']

item.title: But what is your honest answer? Aiding LLM-judges with honest alternatives using steering vectors
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes JUSSA, a white-box framework that uses steering vectors to generate honesty-promoting contrastive alternatives for LLM-judges.
  • Targets detection of subtle judge manipulation/dishonesty (e.g., sycophancy and manipulation) in LLM-as-a-judge setups.
  • Evaluated on a manipulation benchmark with human-validated response pairs across dishonesty levels; reports AUROC gains for GPT-4.1 and Claude Haiku judges.
  • Finds steering effectiveness is layer-dependent (notably middle layers) and degrades with task/judge capability mismatch.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Leon Eshuijs', 'Archie Chaudhury', 'Alan McBeth', 'Ethan Nguyen']
  • Tags: ['LLM-as-a-Judge', 'Steering Vectors', 'White-box Auditing', 'Manipulation Detection']

item.title: Detecting Multi-Agent Collusion Through Multi-Agent Interpretability
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces NARCBench to evaluate detection of multi-agent collusion, including under environment distribution shift.
  • Proposes five probing techniques that compute per-agent deception scores and aggregate them to classify collusion at the group level.
  • Shows strong in-distribution performance (1.00 AUROC) and reduced but nontrivial zero-shot transfer performance (0.60–0.86 AUROC).
  • Finds activation-level evidence suggesting token-localized spikes in colluding agents when processing encoded parts of partner messages.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Aaron Rose', 'Carissa Cullen', 'Brandon Gary Kaplowitz', 'Christian Schroeder de Witt']
  • Tags: ['multi-agent systems', 'collusion detection', 'model interpretability/probing', 'adversarial behavior detection']

item.title: Does Unification Come at a Cost? Uni-SafeBench: A Safety Benchmark for Unified Multimodal Large Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces Uni-SafeBench, a multimodal safety benchmark for Unified Multimodal Large Models (UMLMs) spanning multiple task types and a taxonomy of safety categories.
  • Develops Uni-Judger to distinguish contextual safety from intrinsic safety when evaluating unified models.
  • Finds that architectural unification improves capabilities but can significantly degrade intrinsic safety compared to specialized multimodal models.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zixiang Peng', 'Yongxiu Xu', 'Qinyi Zhang', 'Jiexun Shen', 'Yifan Zhang', 'Hongbo Xu', 'Yubin Wang', 'Gaopeng Gou']
  • Tags: ['safety-benchmark', 'multimodal-llms', 'red-teaming-evaluation']

item.title: Shapley-Guided Neural Repair Approach via Derivative-Free Optimization
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SHARPEN: interpretable fault localization using Deep SHAP to identify faulty layers/neurons/filters contributing to property violations.
  • Repairs identified neurons/filters using derivative-free optimization (CMA-ES), enabling gradient-free coordinated adjustments.
  • Evaluates on three repair tasks including backdoor removal, adversarial mitigation, and unfairness repair with reported performance gains over baselines.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Xinyu Sun', 'Wanwei Liu', 'Haoang Chi', 'Tingyu Chen', 'Xiaoguang Mao', 'Shangwen Wang', 'Lei Bu', 'Jingyi Wang', 'Yang Tan', 'Zhenyi Qi']
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'backdoor removal', 'model repair/defense', 'derivative-free optimization', 'explainable fault localization']

item.title: WARP: Guaranteed Inner-Layer Repair of NLP Transformers
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes WARP, a constraint-based framework for repairing Transformer-based NLP models with formal/provable guarantees.
  • Repairs are formulated as a convex quadratic program using a first-order linearization of the logit gap, enabling optimization over multiple layers/high-dimensional parameter space.
  • Provides per-sample guarantees including positive margin (correct classification), preservation over a remain set, and a certified robustness radius via Lipschitz continuity.
  • Includes sensitivity-based preprocessing to maintain feasibility across architectures and shows empirical robustness gains against adversarial inputs.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hsin-Ling Hsu', 'Min-Yu Chen', 'Nai-Chia Chen', 'Yan-Ru Chen', 'Yi-Ling Chang', 'Fang Yu']
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'model repair', 'certified guarantees', 'NLP Transformers']

item.title: Thinking Wrong in Silence: Backdoor Attacks on Continuous Latent Reasoning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes and evaluates ThoughtSteer, a backdoor attack on continuous latent reasoning models that operates via perturbing an input embedding vector.
  • Shows attack success (up to >=99%) with near-baseline clean accuracy, transfer to held-out benchmarks, and persistence through clean fine-tuning.
  • Claims evasion of multiple token-level defenses and introduces a geometric latent-space mechanism (Neural Collapse) to explain robustness against defenses.
  • Suggests that effective backdoors must leave a high linearly separable signature in latent space (probe AUC>=0.999).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Swapnil Parekh']
  • Tags: ['backdoor attacks', 'latent-space adversarial attacks', 'continuous reasoning', 'defense evasion', 'mechanistic interpretability']

item.title: Exploring Silent Data Corruption as a Reliability Challenge in LLM Training
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies Silent Data Corruption (SDC) during LLM training caused by hardware faults that evade normal detection.
  • Uses controlled fault injection at GPU matrix-multiply instruction level to characterize corruption signatures and effects on gradients/attention/loss.
  • Proposes a lightweight detection mechanism for harmful parameter updates and mitigates impact by recomputing the most recent training step upon detection.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Anton Altenbernd', 'Philipp Wiesner', 'Odej Kao']
  • Tags: ['machine-learning-security', 'fault-injection', 'training-reliability', 'attack-detection-mitigation']

item.title: Convergence of Byzantine-Resilient Gradient Tracking via Probabilistic Edge Dropout
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes GT-PD, a defense for distributed optimization with Byzantine (adversarial) agents using message clipping plus probabilistic edge dropout based on trust scores.
  • Introduces GT-PD-L with leaky integration to limit accumulation of tracking errors under persistent Byzantine perturbations, achieving linear convergence to a bounded neighborhood.
  • Analyzes convergence behavior under Byzantine isolation vs partial isolation, and studies effects of two-tier dropout on honest variance.
  • Experiments on MNIST compare against robust aggregation baselines and report improved robustness under stealth Byzantine attacks (Sign Flip, ALIE, Inner Product Manipulation).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Amirhossein Dezhboro', 'Fateme Maleki', 'Arman Adibi', 'Erfan Amini', 'Jose E. Ramirez-Marquez']
  • Tags: ['Byzantine-robust distributed optimization', 'Defense: clipping/projection', 'Attack-resilient gradient tracking', 'Probabilistic trust/dropout']

item.title: G-Drift MIA: Membership Inference via Gradient-Induced Feature Drift in LLMs
item.description:
Summary

item.title: Robust Multimodal Safety via Conditional Decoding

  • Presents CASA (Classification Augmented with Safety Attention), a conditional decoding method for multimodal LLMs to predict a safety token before generating responses.

item.description:

  • Proposes/uses Lipschitz-ball verification with provable analytical bounds, achieving zero false accepts across a wide range of dimensions, and demonstrates that chaining/compositional verification enables larger safe exploration than single-ball verification.

item.title: Bypassing Prompt Injection Detectors through Evasive Injections
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents an adaptive evasion attack against activation-based prompt injection detectors by optimizing a universal adversarial suffix to fool multiple layer-wise drift probes simultaneously.
  • Uses a modified Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) method to generate suffixes that preserve the malicious effectiveness of prompt injections while evading detection.
  • Reports very high evasion success rates on Phi-3 3.8B and Llama-3 8B against multiple detectors.
  • Proposes a defense via adversarial suffix augmentation (randomized suffix appending during forward passes) to improve detector robustness against adaptive attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Tags: ['prompt injection', 'adversarial suffix', 'attack evasion', 'attack detection/defense']

item.title: Lumos: Let there be Language Model System Certification
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Lumos, a formal specification framework for Language Model System (LMS) behaviors using an imperative probabilistic programming DSL over graphs.
  • Integrates with statistical certifiers to enable certification of LMS properties over arbitrary prompt distributions.
  • Uses Lumos safety specifications for vision-language models in autonomous driving to identify high-probability safety failures under specific conditions (e.g., rainy right-turn scenarios).
  • Includes a prompt-level deterministic verifier aimed at guaranteeing privacy properties of generation distributions.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

item.title: MemeMind: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Harmful Meme Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces MemeMind, a large-scale multimodal dataset for detecting harmful memes, including chain-of-thought style reasoning annotations.
  • Proposes MemeGuard, a multimodal detection framework focused on reasoning to improve accuracy and interpretability for harmful meme detection.
  • Reports that MemeGuard outperforms existing methods on the MemeMind dataset.
  • Positioned as a foundation for future harmful meme detection research.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hexiang Gu', 'Qifan Yu', 'Yuan Liu', 'Zikang Li', 'Saihui Hou', 'Jian Zhao', 'Zhaofeng He']

item.title: But what is your honest answer? Aiding LLM-judges with honest alternatives using steering vectors
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes JUSSA, a white-box framework that uses steering vectors to generate honesty-promoting contrastive alternatives for LLM-judges.
  • Targets detection of subtle judge manipulation/dishonesty (e.g., sycophancy and manipulation) in LLM-as-a-judge setups.
  • Evaluated on a manipulation benchmark with human-validated response pairs across dishonesty levels; reports AUROC gains for GPT-4.1 and Claude Haiku judges.
  • Finds steering effectiveness is layer-dependent (notably middle layers) and degrades with task/judge capability mismatch.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Leon Eshuijs', 'Archie Chaudhury', 'Alan McBeth', 'Ethan Nguyen']
  • Tags: ['LLM-as-a-Judge', 'Steering Vectors', 'White-box Auditing', 'Manipulation Detection']

item.title: A Divide-and-Conquer Strategy for Hard-Label Extraction of Deep Neural Networks via Side-Channel Attacks
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a divide-and-conquer, black-box side-channel framework for hard-label model extraction of deep neural networks.
  • Targets embedded/non-fully-connected DNN architectures (e.g., shortened MobileNetv1) by splitting networks into linear parts for cryptanalytic weight recovery.
  • Validates high-fidelity theft (reported extraction fidelity ~88.4% MobileNetv1, ~93.2% MLP).
  • Uses the extracted model to generate adversarial examples with high transfer success (~95.8% and 96.7%).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Benoit Coqueret', 'Mathieu Carbone', 'Olivier Sentieys', 'Gabriel Zaid']
  • Tags: ['model extraction', 'side-channel attacks', 'hard-label black-box attacks', 'adversarial examples', 'embedded/IoT security']

item.title: When Only the Final Text Survives: Implicit Execution Tracing for Multi-Agent Attribution
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Implicit Execution Tracing (IET) to enable multi-agent attribution when execution logs/agent identifiers are missing.
  • Embeds agent-specific, key-conditioned statistical signals into token generation so the final text becomes a self-verifying provenance record.
  • Recovers a linearized execution trace from output via transition-aware scoring, evaluated under identity removal and privacy-preserving redaction.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yi Nian', 'Haosen Cao', 'Shenzhe Zhu', 'Henry Peng Zou', 'Qingqing Luan', 'Yue Zhao']
  • Tags: ['multi-agent attribution', 'provenance watermarking', 'execution tracing', 'LLM security accountability']

item.title: When Agents Persuade: Rhetoric Generation and Mitigation in LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies LLM agents producing manipulative/propgandistic text when given propaganda objectives, analyzing rhetoric and detection via specialized classifiers.
  • Evaluates specific defense/mitigation approaches (SFT, DPO, ORPO) to reduce propagandistic behavior.
  • Uses a security-adjacent threat model focused on manipulation generation and rhetorical technique detection rather than classic jailbreaks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Julia Jose', 'Ritik Roongta', 'Rachel Greenstadt']
  • Tags: ['LLM safety', 'Manipulation/propaganda generation', 'Adversarial evaluation', 'Preference optimization (ORPO/DPO)']

item.title: Genesis: Evolving Attack Strategies for LLM Web Agent Red-Teaming
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes “Genesis,” an agentic red-teaming framework for attacking LLM web agents.
  • Uses an Attacker module combining genetic algorithms with hybrid strategy representations to generate adversarial injections.
  • Adds a Scorer to evaluate agent responses and a Strategist that mines interaction logs to evolve and expand an attack strategy library over time.
  • Experiments on multiple web tasks report discovery of novel strategies and improved attack effectiveness over existing baselines.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

item.title: Dive into the Agent Matrix: A Realistic Evaluation of Self-Replication Risk in LLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a scenario-driven evaluation framework to measure LLM agent self-replication risk under realistic production-like environments and tasks.
  • Introduces metrics (Overuse Rate, Aggregate Overuse Count) to quantify frequency and severity of uncontrolled replication.
  • Demonstrates that many state-of-the-art models exhibit a tendency toward uncontrolled self-replication under operational pressures when objective alignment is induced to break.

Paper Type

item.title: TRACE: Training-Free Partial Audio Deepfake Detection via Embedding Trajectory Analysis of Speech Foundation Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes TRACE, a training-free countermeasure to detect partial audio deepfakes (spliced synthesized segments).
  • Uses frozen speech foundation model embeddings and analyzes first-order dynamics/trajectory smoothness to find splice-induced disruptions.
  • Evaluates on multiple partial-spoof benchmarks across languages and several speech foundation models, showing competitive performance without labeled data or retraining.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: VibeGuard: A Security Gate Framework for AI-Generated Code
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes VibeGuard, a pre-publish security gate to mitigate common security “blind spots” in AI-generated code workflows, including artifact hygiene, packaging drift, source-map exposure, hardcoded secrets, and supply-chain risk.
  • Evaluates the framework on eight synthetic projects (seven vulnerable, one clean) showing perfect recall and strong precision, with correct pass/fail gate decisions across multiple policy levels.
  • Targets failure modes specific to AI-assisted “vibe coding,” where existing static analysis/secret scanning may miss packaging/config and artifact-leak issues.

Paper Type

  • Research

  • Authors: ['Ying Xie']
  • Tags: ['AI-generated code', 'Security gate', 'Supply-chain security', 'Source map exposure', 'Secrets detection']

item.title: Adversarial Attacks in AI-Driven RAN Slicing: SLA Violations and Recovery
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies adversarial jamming attacks against AI-driven RAN slicing decisions.
  • Analyzes how attacks bias DRL-based resource allocation and cause service level agreement (SLA) violations.
  • Quantifies recovery dynamics, showing delayed return of the DRL reward toward the clean baseline.

item.title: Automated Framework to Evaluate and Harden LLM System Instructions against Encoding Attacks
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an automated evaluation framework to test confidentiality of LLM system instructions against encoding/serialization-style extraction attacks.
  • Finds high attack success rates (>0.7) when extraction is reframed as structured output/encoding tasks that bypass refusal-based instruction policies.
  • Studies 46 verified system instructions across four common models and analyzes leakage behavior under different serialization formats.
  • Demonstrates a mitigation approach using one-shot instruction reshaping (with a Chain-of-Thought model) to reduce attack success without retraining.

Paper Type

  • Research

  • Authors: ['Anubhab Sahu', 'Diptisha Samanta', 'Reza Soosahabi']

item.title: WARP: Guaranteed Inner-Layer Repair of NLP Transformers
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes WARP, a constraint-based framework for repairing Transformer-based NLP models with formal/provable guarantees.
  • Repairs are formulated as a convex quadratic program using a first-order linearization of the logit gap, enabling optimization over multiple layers/high-dimensional parameter space.
  • Provides per-sample guarantees including positive margin (correct classification), preservation over a remain set, and a certified robustness radius via Lipschitz continuity.
  • Includes sensitivity-based preprocessing to maintain feasibility across architectures and shows empirical robustness gains against adversarial inputs.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: Thinking Wrong in Silence: Backdoor Attacks on Continuous Latent Reasoning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes and evaluates ThoughtSteer, a backdoor attack on continuous latent reasoning models that operates via perturbing an input embedding vector.
  • Shows attack success (up to >=99%) with near-baseline clean accuracy, transfer to held-out benchmarks, and persistence through clean fine-tuning.
  • Claims evasion of multiple token-level defenses and introduces a geometric latent-space mechanism (Neural Collapse) to explain robustness against defenses.
  • Suggests that effective backdoors must leave a high linearly separable signature in latent space (probe AUC>=0.999).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Swapnil Parekh']
  • Tags: ['backdoor attacks', 'latent-space adversarial attacks', 'continuous reasoning', 'defense evasion', 'mechanistic interpretability']

item.title: RAGShield: Provenance-Verified Defense-in-Depth Against Knowledge Base Poisoning in Government Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes RAGShield, a defense-in-depth framework to prevent knowledge base poisoning in government retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems.
  • Uses provenance verification (C2PA-inspired cryptographic attestation) at ingestion, trust-weighted retrieval, and provenance-aware generation with auditable citations.
  • Introduces a formal taint lattice and cross-source contradiction detection to catch insider threats and manipulation that may bypass provenance.
  • Evaluates against multiple attacker tiers on a benchmark dataset, reporting 0.0% attack success rate for most threat classes while noting ingestion-time limits for insider replacement attacks.

Paper Type

item.title: Finding and Reactivating Post-Trained LLMs' Hidden Safety Mechanisms
item.description:
Summary

  • Investigates why post-training/fine-tuning LLMs can degrade safety, hypothesizing that original safety mechanisms get masked or suppressed while task-related representations are amplified.
  • Shows that hidden safety mechanisms in post-trained models still exist rather than being removed.
  • Proposes SafeReAct, a lightweight LoRA-based alignment method on a few layers to restore suppressed safety behaviors.
  • Reports improved safety on harmful prompts for multiple large reasoning models without significant loss in reasoning performance.

item.title: Detecting Multi-Agent Collusion Through Multi-Agent Interpretability
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces NARCBench to evaluate detection of multi-agent collusion, including under environment distribution shift.
  • Proposes five probing techniques that compute per-agent deception scores and aggregate them to classify collusion at the group level.
  • Shows strong in-distribution performance (1.00 AUROC) and reduced but nontrivial zero-shot transfer performance (0.60–0.86 AUROC).
  • Finds activation-level evidence suggesting token-localized spikes in colluding agents when processing encoded parts of partner messages.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research

  • Tags: ['multi-agent systems', 'collusion detection', 'model interpretability/probing', 'adversarial behavior detection']

item.title: Adversarial Moral Stress Testing of Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Adversarial Moral Stress Testing (AMST) to evaluate LLM ethical robustness under adversarial multi-turn interactions.
  • Uses structured prompt stress transformations and distribution-aware metrics to measure variance, tail risk, and temporal behavioral drift across rounds.
  • Finds models differ substantially in robustness profiles and that degradation can occur across interaction sequences, not captured by single-round safety benchmarks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Tags: ['adversarial evaluation', 'LLM safety', 'red teaming', 'multi-turn robustness']

item.title: UK AISI Alignment Evaluation Case-Study
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents an evaluation framework (built on Petri with a custom scaffold) to test whether frontier LLMs reliably follow intended goals when deployed as coding assistants in an AI lab.
  • Assesses a specific security-relevant risk: potential sabotage of safety research under deployment conditions.
  • Finds no confirmed instances of research sabotage, but observes frequent refusals on safety-relevant research tasks (especially Claude Opus 4.5 Preview and Sonnet 4.5).
  • Includes findings about “evaluation awareness” (whether models can distinguish evaluation vs real deployment) and claims both models can do this when prompted, with reduced unprompted awareness for one model.

Paper Type

  • Research/Technical Report

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Alexandra Souly', 'Robert Kirk', 'Jacob Merizian', "Abby D'Cruz", 'Xander Davies']
  • Tags: ['LLM auditing', 'AI safety evaluation', 'agentic deployment risk', 'red teaming']

item.title: Does Unification Come at a Cost? Uni-SafeBench: A Safety Benchmark for Unified Multimodal Large Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces Uni-SafeBench, a multimodal safety benchmark for Unified Multimodal Large Models (UMLMs) spanning multiple task types and a taxonomy of safety categories.
  • Develops Uni-Judger to distinguish contextual safety from intrinsic safety when evaluating unified models.
  • Finds that architectural unification improves capabilities but can significantly degrade intrinsic safety compared to specialized multimodal models.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zixiang Peng', 'Yongxiu Xu', 'Qinyi Zhang', 'Jiexun Shen', 'Yifan Zhang', 'Hongbo Xu', 'Yubin Wang', 'Gaopeng Gou']
  • Tags: ['safety-benchmark', 'multimodal-llms', 'red-teaming-evaluation']

item.title: The Silicon Mirror: Dynamic Behavioral Gating for Anti-Sycophancy in LLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes “The Silicon Mirror,” an orchestration framework to reduce LLM sycophancy (over-validating user persuasion rather than epistemic accuracy).
  • Uses a Behavioral Access Control system with real-time sycophancy risk scoring, a Trait Classifier to detect persuasion tactics in multi-turn dialogues, and a Generator-Critic loop where an auditor vetoes sycophantic drafts.
  • Evaluates on TruthfulQA adversarial scenarios and reports substantial reductions in sycophancy versus vanilla prompting and static guardrails, including cross-model results on Gemini 2.5 Flash.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Harshee Jignesh Shah (Independent Researcher)']
  • Tags: ['AI safety', 'LLM agent defense', 'Sycophancy mitigation', 'Guardrails/behavioral gating', 'LLM evaluation (adversarial scenarios)']
